title: Comparison-Free Bit-Stream Generation for Cost-Efficient Unary Computing
problem: Converting binary radix data to unary representation via comparator-based generators incurs high area and power cost, especially as input count and precision increase.
motivation: Unary computing offers simplicity and noise tolerance advantages, but the conversion bottleneck limits practical adoption in hardware designs.
method: Proposes low-cost comparison-free unary number generation mechanism avoiding comparators entirely. Introduces serial and two parallel (exact and approximate) unary generator designs using alternative conversion logic.
key_novelty: Comparison-free unary number generation eliminating comparator overhead in binary-to-unary conversion.
contributions: Reduced hardware area vs comparator-based converters
Two parallel generator variants (exact and approximate) for different use cases
limitations: Not discussed; limited details on area/power quantification.
primary_theme: Comparison-free unary number generation for efficient data conversion
